findings_to_judge.finding: The 'digital asset treasury' behind the 2026-08-04 buyback announcement is majority-encumbered: at 2026-03-31 Canaan owned only 802.6 bitcoins outright (plus 63.4 held as customer deposits), while 905.0 bitcoins were pledged for secured term loans and 100.0 more were transferred into a fixed-term product, against US$54.5m of loans (US$21.14m current + US$33.37m long-term).

Canaan's funded forward order book has not been rebuilt: contract liabilities (customer advances) were US$7.739m at 2026-03-31 and US$9.317m at 2025-12-31, against 'nearly $87 million' at 2025-09-30 when over 85% came from North American clients - and no new Avalon purchase-order press release has appeared at any point between June and September 2026.

Q2 exit-rate was artificially crushed and has already fully recovered: non-JV month-end operating hashrate was 3.36 EH/s against 10.05 EH/s installed at 2026-06-30 (grid maintenance, on top of a 'planned expiration of a hosting agreement' in May that cut non-JV installed capacity from 266.3 MW in April to 246.2 MW), and by 2026-07-31 non-JV operating was back to 10.05 EH/s - equal to installed - with the average revenue split improving from 60.3% to 60.6%.

Inventory of US$139.1m at 2026-03-31 sits against a Q2 revenue guide of US$35-45m and a Q1 gross LOSS of US$22.9m on US$62.7m of revenue, while the current-generation Avalon A16 (12.8 J/TH, launched October 2025) leaves the A15-era stock as the write-down candidate - Canaan's own self-mining fleet is still running at 23.7 J/TH global and 17.9 J/TH in North America.

Sell-side numbers for CAN were never marked down to Canaan's own guidance: the terminal Q2 revenue consensus is $53.87-55.41m against the company's 19-May guide of $35-45m, and FY2026 consensus of $269.23m (6 analysts, S&P Global, as of 2026-07-24) requires H2 revenue ~65% above an H1 that will total roughly $98-108m — so both the Q2 headline and any Q3 guide mechanically print as a large 'miss', and investing.com's feed has already auto-published a Q2 revenue 'actual' of $31.20m vs $55.41m consensus (below the low end of guidance) in an article timestamped 2026-09-03 06:27.

The liquidity line is the print's real unknown: cash fell from $80.8m at 2025-12-31 to $43.5m at 2026-03-31 (a $37.3m burn in one quarter) against $106.4m of current liabilities and $21.1m of loans due inside a year, 905 of 1,871 bitcoins were pledged as collateral for $54.5m of secured term loans, and Q2 revenue was guided 30-45% lower than Q1 — so the 30-June balance sheet, struck with BTC at $58,504 on 2026-06-30 (BTC's worst quarter in years, -34% YTD), is where the market first sees how little unencumbered liquidity is left behind the '$130m treasury' headline.

The stated trigger for the crypto-funded buyback has been extinguished by the rally it helped cause: on 2026-08-04 Canaan justified monetising digital assets by saying it was 'trading below the combined value of its digital assets holdings and its cash and cash equivalents as reported on March 31, 2026' ($130m treasury as of 3 August plus $43.5m cash = $173.5m, against a $144.7m market cap on 6 August), but after a 108.8% August the market cap is $261.0m while the treasury of 1,917 BTC and 3,952 ETH is worth roughly $165m at BTC ~$81.0k and ETH ~$2.4-2.5k — so on the company's own yardstick the stock now trades at roughly a 25% premium rather than a 17% discount, and the repurchase authorisation expires 2026-12-12.

The Nasdaq minimum-bid arithmetic is now impossible without a capital-structure action: the ADS must close at or above $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days by 2027-01-11, which from $0.3501 is +186%, so an ADS ratio change (currently 1 ADS = 15 Class A ordinary shares) has to be noticed to holders around November to be effective in time — and the 8 September call is the first scheduled management appearance since the deadline was granted.
